clue.text: In church, religious leader has. right to be more awkward

indicators.note: In tells us the leader sits inside the letters for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation

explanation.surface: A rabbi visiting a church claims the right to be difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts RABBI inside CE, giving CRABBIE, and R follows. The stray full stop after 'has' is a newspaper print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means grumpy or awkward, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Accountant has a number, of dogs

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
nine is a number

explanation.surface: An accountant owns several dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to dogs, as canine teeth are dog-like teeth.

clue.text: Married woman drops right under car — she acts without thinking

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under comes after the car word

parts.note: auto is a short word for a car

indicators.note: drops means the letter for right falls out of the married woman's word

parts.note: a matron is a married woman

explanation.surface: A wife lets go of the wheel in the car and drives on autopilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes R from MATRON to leave MATON, which goes 'under' AUTO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot-like person who behaves mechanically, by reflex rather than thought, is called this.

clue.text: Cricketer snatches run — a single — for the title

indicators.note: snatches means the cricketer's word grabs and holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a single is one

explanation.surface: A batsman steals a quick single in a match with a trophy at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snatches' puts R + ONE inside BAT. A BAT is crossword shorthand for a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary British rank below a baron, carrying the style Sir, is a title.

clue.text: Exceed 40, say

indicators.note: say signals that the letters for forty are spoken out loud

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Going beyond forty, perhaps in age or speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as letters, 'X L' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outdo others is a synonym of going beyond them.

clue.text: Buttonhole for Bill Price

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
cost is price

explanation.surface: A request for the invoice and price of a buttonhole flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttonhole' looks like a flower for a lapel; here it is the verb meaning to stop someone and talk at them.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone and speak to them insistently, as a buttonholer does, is a synonym.

clue.text: Allotting part of a fisherman's work

explanation.surface: An angler handing out roles in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigning roles to actors is one sense; throwing a line or net into water is the angler's other sense.

clue.text: Conclude work in the Orient

parts.note: OP is opus, a musical work
taken as written
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Wrapping up a job in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclude' is meant in the sense of stating a view, not finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude in the sense of state an opinion or judge is a synonym.

clue.text: Not quite the earth .perhaps certain it's worth a lot

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the shortened letters may be arranged another way
not quite means the word earth stops short of its final letter

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A thing not quite as precious as the whole world, yet surely valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims EARTH to EART, which 'perhaps' rearranges to TREA before SURE. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything prized as highly valuable is called this, as a national treasure is.

clue.text: A trick indeed when troops are so spread out

indicators.note: the first two letters of indeed, read apart, say the trick goes inside the deed

parts.note: taken as written
a ploy is a trick

explanation.surface: A military trick that works when troops are dispersed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits into 'in deed': PLOY goes inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops positioned across an area for action are said to be this way.

clue.text: Fruit, biscuit and dessert, say, with music

parts.note: a nut is a kind of fruit
a cracker is a savoury biscuit

indicators.note: say signals that the pudding word is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a sweet is the British word for a pudding course

explanation.surface: A menu listing fruit, biscuits and pudding, served with music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' (British for dessert) said aloud gives SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet music drawn from his Christmas score is the piece named.

clue.text: The venom in a lizard is not' altogether insignificant

indicators.note: not altogether means only part of the phrase venom in a lizard is used

explanation.surface: A lizard's venom is somewhat harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'not' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal fee is a token, trivially small one, so the word means slight or minor.

clue.text: Hangs about in Estoril resort

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, means the letters of Estoril are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: Someone idles around the Portuguese seaside resort of Estoril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place (Estoril is one); it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering or idling somewhere without purpose is a synonym.

clue.text: These figures make USA ratty

indicators.note: make signals that the letters of USA ratty are made into something new

explanation.surface: Some statues so ugly they annoy America.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectively, sculpted figures are known by this word.

clue.text: Equipment 'for. Sandhurst-soldiers in mounted army.

indicators.note: in places the academy and soldiers inside the army letters
in a down clue mounted means the army letters climb, so they read upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army
RMA is the Royal Military Academy at Sandhurst
men are soldiers

explanation.surface: Kit issued to Sandhurst cadets in the cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' reverses TA to AT, which goes round RMA + MEN. Sandhurst is Britain's officer academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Military weapons and gear are equipment for fighting.

clue.text: Gorge the king with fish.

parts.note: a gap is a gorge or ravine
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A king gorges himself on fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb about eating; it is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is a type of fish, also called a comber or sea perch.

clue.text: Declare it, say, to be above the church'

indicators.note: in a down clue being above means the first piece sits over the church

parts.note: it is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A ruling that something ranks above the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To state formally or officially, as a judge pronounces sentence, is a synonym.

clue.text: Tells of one — sapper's discomfiture

indicators.note: discomfiture means the letters of one and sapper's are thrown into disarray

parts.note: I is one
taken as written with its S

explanation.surface: A soldier's embarrassment is told to others.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise is to inform someone of something.

clue.text: Marine ape

explanation.surface: A sea-soldier who resembles an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: British forces slang for a soldier or marine is one sense; the orang-utan genus name is the other.

clue.text: Short' version of Lonsdale's play for examination

indicators.note: a short version means the play's title is clipped at its end

parts.note: Frederick Lonsdale wrote the comedy On Approval

explanation.surface: An abridged Lonsdale play being reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Lonsdale's 1927 comedy is clipped of its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods taken home on trial, returnable if unwanted, are sent this way for inspection.

clue.text: Many a journalist grabs a man from ACAS

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, many

indicators.note: grabs means the journalist's word takes hold of the second a

parts.note: an editor is a journalist

explanation.surface: Lots of reporters chase a conciliation official.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is Britain's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which settles labour disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between in industrial disputes, as ACAS staff act, is a conciliator.

clue.text: Bad pain, sir? Not if you take this

definitions.text: Bad pain, sir? Not if you take this

indicators.note: bad means the letters of pain and sir go wrong and are reordered

explanation.surface: A doctor tells a patient a pill will stop the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling pill stops a bad pain, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Suit for beaters.

explanation.surface: A suit worn by grouse-shoot beaters.
explanation.definitionFit: One card-game suit is one sense; organs that beat in the chest are the other.

clue.text: Engineers demand salvage

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
claim means demand

explanation.surface: Engineers demand payment for salvage.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or rescue something, as land is taken back from the sea, is to salvage it.

clue.text: Applause for the poet, always upholding honour

indicators.note: in a down clue upholding means the second piece holds the honour up from below

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A poet is always cheered when honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholding' puts EER beneath CH in this down entry. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of approval or applause is one.

clue.text: Assume superior attitude

parts.note: sup is an abbreviation of superior
a pose is an attitude

explanation.surface: Take on an air of superiority.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something as true without proof is a synonym.

clue.text: Fish pie, say, in the Mediterranean.

indicators.note: in places the reworked pie inside the sea

parts.note: the Mediterranean is a sea

indicators.note: say here loosely signals pie given in another form

explanation.surface: A fish pie made in a Mediterranean country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' reworks PIE to EPI, which goes inside SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the cuttlefish genus, and the creature is loosely called a fish.

clue.text: He's no manager, though a capital contributor

definitions.text: He's no manager, though a capital contributor

parts.words: He's no manager, though a capital contributor
parts.note: capital looks like praise for a contribution but means money invested; the investor plays no part in running the firm

explanation.surface: A non-executive who is nonetheless splendid company.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor in a business who takes no active role in management is this.

clue.text: Address heard night and day

annotationWithheld.why: Address heard night and day (6), SERMON: no parse found for 'heard night and day'; the homophone of SIR plus MON leaves 'night' unexplained

clue.text: Not/ hurting like Marie Antoinette's poor people?

explanation.surface: French peasants unharmed despite the queen's indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIN is French for bread: Marie Antoinette's poor were breadless, told to eat cake instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing no hurt is one sense; lacking bread, pain in French, is the punning other sense.
